item.title: Sumsets regularity versus Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity for monomial curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.24121v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $A=\{0=a_0<a_1<\dots<a_{k-1}=d\}$ be integers with greatest common divisor $1$, let $C_A$ be the projective monomial curve they define, and let $\mathrm{reg}(A)$ be the Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity of its coordinate ring. Gimenez and Gonz\'alez-S\'anchez proved $\mathrm{reg}(A)\le\sigma(A)+1$ for the sumsets regularity $\sigma(A)$; the reverse inequality $\sigma(A)\le\mathrm{reg}(A)$ was proposed as an open conjecture in a 2024 talk. We show that it fails and measure by how much. Let $c_1,c_2$ be the conductors of the two numerical semigroups attached to $A$ and $N=\lceil(c_1+c_2)/d\rceil$. For curves in $\mathbb{P}^3$ that are not arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay, $\mathrm{reg}(A)\ge(c_1+c_2)/d+2$, with equality exactly for the arithmetically Buchsbaum curves, and $\sigma(A)=\mathrm{reg}(A)$. For arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay curves in $\mathbb{P}^3$ we prove $9N\le10\,\mathrm{reg}(A)-2$, with $9/10$ best possible, and give an explicit family with $\sigma(A)-\mathrm{reg}(A)$ unbounded. In $\mathbb{P}^4$ a family with a band-shaped Ap\'ery set has $\mathrm{reg}(A)/\sigma(A)\to(2+\sqrt2)/4$ along the solutions of a Pell equation, and gluing carries this bound to every $\mathbb{P}^r$ with $r\ge5$.
item.dc:creator: Prashant Chaudhary, Kapil Khandelwal

item.title: Bounded powers of edge ideals: Nearly Gorenstein polytopes
item.description: arXiv:2610.24438v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A lattice polytope $\mathcal{P} \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ of dimension $n$ is called nearly Gorenstein if $\mathcal{P}$ is normal and if its Ehrhart ring is a nearly Gorenstein ring. We study nearly Gorenstein polytopes arising from discrete polymatroids of bounded powers of edge ideals. Especially, it is shown that every nearly Gorenstein polytope coming from either a complete graph or a complete bipartite graph is level.
item.dc:creator: Takayuki Hibi, Seyed Amin Seyed Fakhari

item.title: Unique Factorization of Power Series Rings over Q-UFDs of Dimension at Most 3
item.description: arXiv:2610.24551v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $R$ be a Noetherian unique factorization domain containing $\mathbb Q$, with $\dim R\leq3$. We prove that $R[[t]]$ is a unique factorization domain if and only if two conditions hold: every two-generated parameter ideal $q$ in every height-two localization satisfies $\overline{q^2}\subseteq q$, and every height-three localization has depth three. No excellence or completion hypothesis is imposed. The main local result is that $A[[t]]$ is not a UFD whenever $A$ is a local $\mathbb Q$-UFD of dimension at least three and depth two. We also prove that the UFD property of $R[[t]]$ passes to every coefficient localization in dimension at most three, give an all-dimensional criterion when the completions of the maximal localizations satisfy Serre's condition $(S_2)$, and obtain an arbitrary-characteristic criterion for excellent UFDs of dimension at most three.
item.dc:creator: Elad Paran

item.title: Every commutative perfect ring is a quotient of an almost perfect domain
item.description: arXiv:2610.24940v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we show that every nonzero commutative perfect ring is a quotient of a one-dimensional semilocal almost perfect domain of characteristic zero. The domain can be chosen to have as many maximal ideals as the given ring has local factors. The construction uses coefficient discrete valuation rings, triangular presentations of purely inseparable residue extensions, and approximation for finitely many independent rank-one valuations. Independent error variables keep the construction inside a field. A normal-form argument shows that the divided elements used to get perfect principal quotients do not kill any further good monomial. In positive residue characteristic, the choice $a=2c+1$ with $c\ge n$ protects the nonzero powers of $p$ in a target ring of characteristic $p^n$. We also give local and mixed-characteristic consequences, and examples with non-nilpotent radicals.
item.dc:creator: Xiaolei Zhang

item.title: Polynomial bounds for the stability of associated primes of monomial ideals
item.description: arXiv:2610.25422v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $I$ be a nonzero proper monomial ideal in ${\rm k}[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$, and let $d$ be the maximal degree of a minimal monomial generator. We prove that the index of stability of the associated primes of its ordinary powers satisfies \[ {\rm astab}(I)\le\frac{(4e)^{r-1}}4\,d^{r-1}\qquad(r\ge3), \] while ${\rm astab}(I)=1$ for $r=2$. If $I$ has $s\ge2$ minimal generators, we also obtain \[ {\rm astab}(I)\le\min\{r,s\}(s-1)d^{\min\{r-1,s-2\}}. \] The first estimate answers Hoa's question on polynomial bounds. The proofs reduce stabilization to integer optimization for a matrix whose last row records the power of the ideal. We bound the degrees of its circuits and Graver basis elements and prove proximity estimates for optimal solutions in fixed fibers. A Steinitz rearrangement and a lattice-point count in the difference body of a simplex give the generator-independent bound. The matrix estimates hold for arbitrary indexed integral configurations in a simplex and real linear objective functions. The stability bounds hold over an arbitrary field, without normality or equigeneration assumptions.
item.dc:creator: Tran Nam Trung

item.title: On the arithmetic rank and cohomological dimension of some residual intersections
item.description: arXiv:2610.25680v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the arithmetic rank and cohomological dimension of each generic residual intersection of the ideal of submaximal Pfaffians of an alternating matrix of variables. This ideal fails to be a set-theoretic complete intersection. Our methods yield several structural results: in characteristic zero, we compute the $D$-module length of the top local cohomology module supported at this ideal and show that over the integers, it admits a $\mathbb{Q}$-vector space structure. In particular, the top local cohomology module has no integer torsion. We also establish the $F$-regularity of the generic residual intersection rings considered here. Further, for each admissible height $s$, we construct $s$-residual intersections of complete intersection ideals and height three Gorenstein ideals that are set-theoretic complete intersections in any characteristic. Finally, we pose a general question of independent interest concerning the behaviour of arithmetic rank.
item.dc:creator: Manav Batavia, Vaibhav Pandey, Uli Walther

item.title: Embedding into quotient
item.description: arXiv:2610.25845v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Bass's finiteness problem for embeddings into proper quotients. Given a commutative ring R, a reduced finitely generated R-algebra A, and an ideal $J\triangleleft A$, we ask whether an R-algebra monomorphism $A\hookrightarrow_R A/J$ forces J=0. We give affirmative answers by presenting two arguments. Also, we discuss not only in the reduced case, but also in several non-reduced cases: when R is artinian and A is finite over R; when R is zero-dimensional and A is finite projective over R; and in a series of Cohen--Macaulay settings. In the module-theoretic direction, for a noetherian reduced ring, and a finitely generated, and torsion-free A-module M, we show that $M\hookrightarrow_R M/JM$ implies that J is contained in a minimal prime of A; if M is faithful, then J=0. Also, dual versions investigated. Examples illustrate the necessity of hypotheses.
item.dc:creator: Mohsen Asgharzadeh, Elham Mahdavi

item.title: Herzog Class of Codimension $3$ Licci Monomial Ideals
item.description: arXiv:2610.26010v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $S$ be the polynomial ring in three variables with homogeneous maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}$. Licci ideals are ideals that can be linked by a finite number of steps to a complete intersection. All licci ideals admit a rigid deformation, and two licci ideals are said to be in the same Herzog class if they have a common rigid deformation. Guerrieri-Ni-Weyman gave a parametrization for the Herzog classes of codimension $3$ licci ideals in terms of pairs of partitions associated to Schur functors. In this paper, we give an explicit formula that determines the Herzog class of a given $\mathfrak{m}$-primary licci monomial ideal.
item.dc:creator: Suhas Vadan Gondi

item.title: Saturation degree of powers of graded ideals
item.description: arXiv:2610.26532v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $I$ be a non-nilpotent graded ideal of a standard graded algebra over a Noetherian commutative ring. We show that the saturation degree sdeg $I^n$ is asymptotically a constant function or a linear function whose slope is one of the generating degrees of $I$. Furthermore, we give sufficient (and necessary) conditions for a numerical functions to be the function sdeg $I^n$ of an ideal $I$ generated by forms of the same degree. Our results may provide a better understanding of the initial behavior of the regularity function reg $I^n$.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Journal of Pure and Applied Algebra 230 (2026), Issue 10, JPAA_108392
item.dc:creator: Le Tuan Hoa, Hop Dang Nguyen, Ngo Viet Trung

item.title: On the classification of threefold flops
item.description: arXiv:2610.24864v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that possibly singular threefold flopping contractions are completely classified by their associated derived contraction algebras, considered up to derived Morita equivalence; in contrast to the smooth case the extra derived structure is necessary in general. This extends previous work of the author on simple flops, and follows from a more general theorem about isolated hypersurface singularities. The key new input is to show that derived localisation at a Hochschild class is Morita invariant; this result raises some interesting questions related to the classification of recollements. We also show that derived contraction algebras admit a deformation-theoretic interpretation in families in a general setting that encompasses threefold flops, flips, and divisor-to-curve contractions.
item.dc:creator: Matt Booth

item.title: Rank and Border Rank Additivity of Complex Tensors with a Hankel Summand
item.description: arXiv:2610.24982v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the CP rank of a complex Hankel tensor of order $m\ge3$ is additive with that of every complex tensor of the same order. Together with the known equality of CP and symmetric ranks for complex Hankel tensors, this yields symmetric rank additivity whenever the other summand has equal CP and symmetric ranks. We also prove that ordinary and symmetric border ranks coincide and are additive on direct sums of complex Hankel tensors of any common order at least three. Their common value is the sum of the middle binary catalecticant ranks. For order three, we further prove border-rank additivity when the other summand has border rank at most three, or is symmetric with at most five essential variables.
item.dc:creator: Jianze Li

item.title: Lefschetz Properties of complete intersesctions and maximal variation of hyperplane sections
item.description: arXiv:2610.25521v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For an artinian complete intersection of forms of degree $d$, we prove that the multiplication by a general linear form is injective up to degree $\frac{3d-1}2$, independently of the number of variables. This is accomplished using algebraic and geometric properties of the union of two complete intersection curves and their general hyperplane sections. As a consequence, we solve, for any $d\ge 4$, the problem about the maximal variation of the hyperplane sections of a smooth hypersurface of degree $d$ posed by A. Beauville.
item.dc:creator: Mats Boij, Juan C. Migliore, Rosa M. Mir\'o-Roig, Uwe Nagel

item.title: Non-existence of negative weight derivations on Jacobian algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.25615v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $S=\mathbb K[x_1,\cdots,x_n]$ be a polynomial ring in $n$ variables with positive integer weights over a field $\mathbb K$ of characteristic zero. Let $f\in S$ be a weighted homogeneous polynomial such that the Jacobian algebra $$A=\left.S \middle/ \left(\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_1},\cdots,\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_n}\right)\right.$$ is a finite-dimensional $\mathbb K$-vector space. We prove that $A$ has no nonzero negative weight derivation, which confirms a conjecture of the third author. An immediate consequence of this conjecture is the micro-local characterization of quasi-homogeneous singularities.
item.dc:creator: Bingyi Chen, Zhiwen Liu, Stephen S. -T. Yau, Huaiqing Zuo

item.title: Twisted logarithmic de Rham complexes and the rational hit conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.26028v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the top degree concentration property for the cohomology of twisted logarithmic de Rham complexes of multiarrangements of hyperplanes. Our main tool is a short exact sequence of twisted logarithmic de Rham complexes based on the deletion-restriction exact sequences for logarithmic differential forms found recently by Abe and Denham. We prove a number of general results that can be used to establish the top degree cohomology concentration property, and also establish that property for some families of multiarrangements. As a consequence of our results, we prove the rational hit conjecture of R.~M.~W.~Wood about the coinvariants of the rational Steenrod algebra acting on the polynomial ring. We also make progress on the deformed version of that conjecture proposed by Hivert and Thi\'ery, prove generalizations of the rational hit conjecture for all complex reflection groups $G(m,p,n)$, thus answering questions of Bergeron, Borie and Thi\'ery, and generalize the rational hit conjecture to all standard subalgebras of the rational Steenrod algebra.
item.dc:creator: Vladimir Dotsenko

item.title: Degree Bounds for Separating Polynomial and Neural Invariants for Point Clouds
item.description: arXiv:2610.26612v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Neural networks that respect the symmetries of point clouds commonly compute high-order representations of the rotation group to improve their expressivity. Such models are known to be universal, and thus able to separate any pair of point clouds, when using representations of sufficiently high order, yet no precise bound on this order, as a function of the number of points, was previously known. We establish the first quadratic lower and upper degree bounds for polynomials that separate point clouds of n points up to rotations and permutations. By showing Tensor Field Networks and MACE can express all invariant polynomials of a given degree with sufficient representation order, we additionally derive the first explicit, quadratic bound on the representation order sufficient for these architectures to be complete, replacing previous existence results with concrete guarantees. We further show that, under local regularity assumptions, point cloud separation can be achieved with a message-passing-based model using invariants whose degree depends only on the size of a local neighborhood, rather than on the size of the full point cloud. Finally, we provide counterexamples showing MACE must compute high order irreducible representations to separate locally regular point clouds.
item.dc:creator: Snir Hordan, Harm Derksen, Mircea Petrache, Nadav Dym

item.title: Huneke's degree-computing problem
item.description: arXiv:1609.04323v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this short note, we deal with a problem posted by Huneke on a numerical invariant attached to symbolic powers of homogenous ideals.
item.dc:creator: Mohsen Asgharzadeh

item.title: On the Rees, Dilworth and Matsumura number
item.description: arXiv:1712.03828v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we study three numerical invariants of local rings: the Rees number, the Dilworth number, and the Matsumura number. These quantities measure, respectively, the minimal lengths of certain cyclic modules, the maximal numbers of generators of ideals, and a parameter-based analogue in higher dimension. We construct a non-exact local complete-intersection ring over $\mathbb{F}_2$, thereby providing a negative answer to a question of Matsumura on the exactness of zero-dimensional complete intersections. We also present a family of artinian Gorenstein local rings over a field of characteristic zero that are exact, making progress on a question of Watanabe. Finally, answering a further question of Matsumura, we introduce and study the Matsumura number and the class of homologically exact rings, which extend the notion of exactness beyond the one-dimensional case.
item.dc:creator: Mohsen Asgharzadeh

item.title: A characterization for the defect of rank one valued field extensions
item.description: arXiv:2210.09157v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we present a characterization for the defect of a simple algebraic extension of rank one valued fields using the key polynomials that define the valuation. As a particular example, this gives the classification of defect extensions of degree $p$ as dependent or independent presented by Kuhlmann.
item.dc:creator: Josnei Novacoski

item.title: The module of K\"ahler differentials for extensions of valuation rings
item.description: arXiv:2307.02315v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The main goal of this paper is to describe the module of K\"ahler differentials for an extension of valuation rings. More precisely, we consider a simple algebraic valued field extension $(L/K,v)$ and the corresponding valuation ring extension $\VR_K\hookrightarrow\VR_L$. In the case when $e(L/K,v)=1$ (and under two additional conditions) we present a characterization of $\Omega_{\VR_L/\VR_K}$ in terms of a given sequence of key polynomials for the extension. We use our main result to present criteria for the equality $\Omega_{\VR_L/\VR_K}=(0)$ to hold.
item.dc:creator: Josnei Novacoski, Mark Spivakovsky

item.title: Minimal limit key polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2311.13558v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we extend the theory of minimal limit key polynomials of valuations on the polynomial ring $\kx$. Minimal key polynomials are useful to describe, for instance, the defect of an extension of valued fields. We use the theory of cuts on ordered abelian groups to show that the previous results on bounded sets of key polynomials of rank one valuations, extend to vertically bounded sets of key polynomials of valuations of an arbitrary rank. We discuss as well properties of minimal limit key polynomials in the vertically unbounded case.
item.dc:creator: Enric Nart, Josnei Novacoski

item.title: Generators for extensions of valuation rings
item.description: arXiv:2401.00182v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a finite valued field extension $(L/K,v)$ we describe the problem of finding sets of generators for the corresponding extension $\VR_L/\VR_K$ of valuation rings. The main tool to obtain such sets are complete sets of (key) polynomials. We show that when the initial index coincides with the ramification index, sequences of key polynomials naturally give rise to sets of generators. We use this to prove Knaf's conjecture for pure extensions.
item.dc:creator: Josnei Novacoski

item.title: Asymptotic behavior of invariants of syzygies of maximal Cohen-Macaulay modules
item.description: arXiv:2412.05860v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: $(A,\mathfrak{m})$ be a complete intersection ring of codimension $c\geq 2$ and dimension $d\geq 1$. Let $M$ be a finitely generated maximal Cohen-Macaulay $A$-module and $M_i=\text{Syz}^A_{i}(M)$ be the $i$-th syzygy of $M$. Let $e^{I}_i(M)$ be the $i$-th Hilbert coefficient of $M$ with respect to an $\mathfrak{m}$-primary ideal $I$. In \cite{Quasipolynomial}, it is proved that the function $i\mapsto e^I_1(M)$ is of quasi-polynomial type with period $2$ and degree $\leq \text{cx}_A(M)-1$, where $\text{cx}_A(M)$ is the complexity of $M.$ We prove that for $I=\mathfrak{m}$, the associated polynomials have the same degree equal to $\text{cx}_A(M)-1$. For $\text{cx}_A(M)=2$ and $j=0,1$, we prove $$\lim_{i\to \infty}\dfrac{e^{\mathfrak{m}}_1(M_{2i+j})}{i}\geq \lim_{i\to \infty}\dfrac{e^{\mathfrak{m}}_0(M_{2i+j})}{i}-\lim_{i\to \infty}\dfrac{\mu(M_{2i+j})}{i}.$$ When equality holds, we prove that the set $\{\text{reg }G_{\mathfrak{m}}(M_i)\,|\, i\geq 0\}$ is bounded, where reg $G_{\mathfrak{m}}(M_i)$ is the Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity of $G_{\mathfrak{m}}(M_i).$
item.dc:creator: Tony J. Puthenpurakal, Samarendra Sahoo

item.title: Valuation rings in simple algebraic extensions of valued fields
item.description: arXiv:2503.09096v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Consider a simple algebraic valued field extension $(L/K,v)$ and denote by $\VR_L$ and $\VR_K$ the corresponding valuation rings. The main goal of this paper is to present, under certain assumptions, a description of $\VR_L$ in terms of generators and relations over $\VR_K$. The main tool used here are complete sequences of key polynomials. It is known that if the ramification index of $(L/K,v)$ is one, then every complete set gives rise to a set of generators of $\VR_L$ over $\VR_K$. We show that we can find a sequence of key polynomials for $(L/K,v)$ which satisfies good properties (called neat). Then we present explicit ``neat" relations that generate all the relations between the corresponding generators of $\VR_L$ over $\VR_K$.
item.dc:creator: Josnei Novacoski, Mark Spivakovsky

item.title: Depth of Artin-Schreier defect towers
item.description: arXiv:2503.18827v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The depth of a simple algebraic extension $(L/K,v)$ of valued fields is the minimal length of the Mac Lane-Vaqui\'e chains of the valuations on $\kx$ determined by the choice of different generators of the extension. In \cite{NN25}, Nart and Novacoski characterized the defectless unibranched extensions of depth one. In this paper, we analyze this problem for towers of Artin-Schreier defect extensions. Under certain conditions on $(K,v)$, we prove that the towers obtained as the compositum of linearly disjoint defect Artin-Schreier extensions of $K$ have depth one. We conjecture that these are the only depth one Artin-Schreier defect towers and we present some examples supporting this conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Enric Nart, Josnei Novacoski

item.title: On the distances of an element to its conjugates
item.description: arXiv:2505.15258v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a valued field $(K,v)$, with a fixed extension of $v$ to the algebraic closure $\overline K$ of $K$, and an algebraic element $\theta\in\overline K$, we study the possible values of $\theta-\theta'$, where $\theta'$ runs through the $K$-conjugates of $\theta$. We compare the number of such values with the depth and the main invariant of $\theta$. Explicit defect examples show that the equalities familiar from the tame case may fail in either direction. We also relate these conjugate distances to ramification ideals of $(K(\theta)/K,v)$ and compute the ramification ideals in several defect extensions.
item.dc:creator: Josnei Novacoski

item.title: Chouinard's formula for $C$-quasi-injective dimension
item.description: arXiv:2511.00684v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The $C$-quasi-injective dimension is a recently introduced homological invariant that unifies and extends the notions of quasi-injective dimension and of injective dimension with respect to a semidualizing module, previously studied by Gheibi and by Takahashi and White, respectively. In the main results of this paper, we provide extensions of the Bass' formula and a version of the Chouinard's formula for modules of finite $C$-quasi-injective dimension over an arbitatry ring.
item.dc:creator: Paulo Martins

item.title: Finiteness of homological dimensions of RHom complexes
item.description: arXiv:2601.07811v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper studies derived Hom complexes with finite projective, Gorenstein projective, or complete intersection dimension over a Noetherian local ring $R$. We establish several stability results concerning finite complete intersection homological dimension of derived Hom complexes. In addition, for $R$-complexes $M$ and $N$ we study when $\operatorname{\textbf{R}Hom}_R(M,N)$ has finite projective, complete intersection dimension or Gorenstein projective dimension under either of the assumptions that $\operatorname{Gpd}_R(N)<\infty$ or $\operatorname{Gid}_R(M)<\infty$. We derive isomorphisms that mimic derived Hom evaluation and derived tensor evaluation when the derived Hom complex has finite Gorenstein projective dimension; while finite projective or complete intersection dimension of the derived Hom complex yields new stability results.
item.dc:creator: Paulo Martins, Victor D. Mendoza Rubio, Zachary Nason

item.title: An infinite series of Gorenstein local algebras failing the affine homogeneity property
item.description: arXiv:2604.04793v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We provide an infinite series of commutative finite-dimensional Gorenstein local algebras $A_n$ for $n \ge 2$. We give an elementary proof that the maximal ideal of every algebra $A_n$ possesses a one-dimensional subspace that is different from the socle and invariant under the automorphism group of $A_n$. The latter implies that the algebras $A_n$ fail the affine homogeneity property. We also discuss some consequences concerning additive actions on projective hypersurfaces, related to the generalized Hassett-Tschinkel correspondence for these algebras.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Mediterranean Journal of Mathematics, vol. 23 (2026), no. 7, article 224
item.dc:creator: Roman Avdeev, Yulia Zaitseva

item.title: A dimension bound towards the Casas-Alvero Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2402.18717v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Casas-Alvero conjecture predicts that every univariate polynomial over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero sharing a common factor with each of its Hasse-Schmidt derivatives is a power of a linear polynomial. The conjecture for polynomials of a fixed degree $n$ is equivalent to the projective variety of such polynomials being one-dimensional. In this paper, we produce dimension bounds for this variety (in degree $n$) over any algebraically closed field of characteristic zero using an arithmetic invariant $B(n)$ of $n$. Consequently for infintely many degrees $n$, we show that the associated arithmetic Casas-Alvero scheme has finitely many rational points over any characteristic zero field. Along the way, we prove several rigidity results towards the conjecture and study arithmetic properties of $B(n)$.
item.dc:creator: Soham Ghosh

item.title: Code Equivalence, Point Set Equivalence, and Polynomial Isomorphism
item.description: arXiv:2511.06843v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The linear code equivalence (LCE) problem is known to be equivalent to the point set equivalence (PSE) problem, i.e., the problem to check whether two sets of points in a projective space over a finite field differ by a linear change of coordinates. For such a point set $\mathbb{X}$, let $R$ be its homogeneous coordinate ring and $\mathfrak{J}_{\mathbb{X}}$ its canonical ideal. Then the LCE problem is shown to be equivalent to an algebra isomorphism problem for the doubling $R/\mathfrak{J}_{\mathbb{X}}$. As this doubling is an Artinian Gorenstein algebra, we can use its Macaulay inverse system to reduce the LCE problem to a Polynomial Isomorphism (PI) problem for homogeneous polynomials. The last step is polynomial time under some mild assumptions about the codes. Moreover, for indecomposable iso-dual codes we can reduce the LCE search problem to the PI search problem of degree 3 by noting that the corresponding point sets are self-associated and arithmetically Gorenstein, so that we can use the isomorphism problem for the Artinian reductions of the coordinate rings and form their Macaulay inverse systems.
item.dc:creator: Martin Kreuzer

item.title: The Homomorphism Submodule Graph
item.description: arXiv:2511.07837v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $M$ be a left $R$-module. We define the \emph{homomorphism submodule graph} $\Gamma_{\mathrm{Hom}}(M)$ as the simple graph whose vertices are the proper submodules of $M$, with an edge between distinct vertices $N_1$ and $N_2$ if and only if $\mathrm{Hom}_R(N_1, M/N_2) \ne 0$ or $\mathrm{Hom}_R(N_2, M/N_1) \ne 0$. This graph encodes homological information about $M$ and reflects its internal structure. We compute $\Gamma_{\mathrm{Hom}}(M)$ for semisimple and uniserial modules, establish precise correspondences between graph-theoretic and algebraic properties, and prove that for modules over Artinian local rings, the isomorphism type of $M$ is determined by $\Gamma_{\mathrm{Hom}}(M)$. We also show that over commutative rings with identity, the graph is always chordal, and we relate its spectral radius to composition length in natural families.
item.dc:creator: Shahram Mehry, Mansour Molaeinejad

item.title: Directed Hamiltonicity in Generalized Kneser Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2511.12553v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that the canonical orientation of the generalized Kneser graph $KG(n,k,s)$ contains a directed Hamiltonian cycle for all integers $s \geq 3$ and $n>sk$. Furthermore, we establish that the dichromatic number of this oriented graph is exactly $k$. As a special case, our results apply to the $s$-stable Kneser graphs $K_{s\text{-stab}}(n,k)$, resolving their directed Hamiltonicity and dichromatic number. Our proof adapts the class graph framework of Ledezma and Pastine to the directed setting, leveraging cyclic rotations and friend class adjacencies to construct a single directed cycle spanning all vertices. This work provides a unified and strengthened perspective on the Hamiltonian properties of Kneser-type graphs.
item.dc:creator: Shahram Mehry

item.title: Splitting vector bundles over real algebraic varieties
item.description: arXiv:2511.15616v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Suppose $X$ is a smooth affine real variety and $\mathscr{E}$ is a vector bundle over $X$. We analyze the problem of splitting off a free rank one summand from $\mathscr{E}$ in corank $0$ and $1$. The problem in corank $0$ can be viewed as the search for a real analog of Murthy's celebrating splitting theorem in the algebraically closed case: to wit, beyond the vanishing of the top Chern class in Chow theory, are the obstructions to splitting ``purely topological''? In a sense, the answer in this case is yes, and we give a proof, using motivic techniques, of a mild extension of the results of Bhatwadekar-Sridharan and Bhatwadekar-Das-Mandal. In corank $1$, in the algebraically closed situation, Murthy's splitting conjecture (now a theorem in characteristic $0$) predicts that the vanishing of the top Chern class in Chow theory is the only obstruction to splitting off a free rank $1$ summand, and we can search for a suitable ``real'' analog of this assertion. We observe that several natural guesses for a ``real'' analog of Murthy's splitting conjecture cannot be true, i.e., that the situation over the real numbers is rather complicated.
item.dc:creator: Aravind Asok, Jean Fasel, Samuel Lerbet

item.title: Cotangent cohomology and higher-order obstructions of matroids
item.description: arXiv:2610.20649v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Matroid Stanley-Reisner rings admit essential deformation obstructions of arbitrarily high order over every field, already at corank three. For each $m\ge3$, we construct a connected cosimple matroid and $m$ fine-homogeneous first-order classes whose proper subcollections integrate jointly and whose pairwise primary cup products vanish. A specified joint $(m-1)$-jet nevertheless has no lift to order $m$, even without preserving the grading. The construction rests on formulas for every multigraded component of the second cotangent cohomology $T^2$ and of its primary cup image, expressed through flats and parallel classes of the dual matroid. These formulas show that $T^2$ vanishes exactly when every connected component has corank at most two, or equivalently when there is no $U_{1,4}$-minor. This proves a conjecture of Constantinescu, Klein, Nguyen, Singh, and Venturello (2025) and characterizes formal smoothness of the affine deformation functor. For the duals of rank-three truncations of $U_{2,m}\oplus U_{2,n}$, $m,n\ge3$, each nonzero homogeneous class modulo the primary cup image is realized as a higher-order obstruction, and the quotient has an explicit presentation with $m+n-2$ minimal homogeneous generators.
